<p class="page-deck">An ongoing conditional, place-based scenario programme for assessing co-benefits and co-costs of climate action while retaining causal, geographical, delivery and valuation assumptions.</p>

**Work type:** Ongoing research programme<br>
**Status:** Ongoing<br>
**Relationship to the lab:** Current CCLL work — Owner-approved current programme of the Cities and Climate Learning Lab.<br>
**Primary theme:** [Consequences for People and Places](/research/consequences-for-people-and-places.html)

## How this work contributes to climate learning

**Primary theme:** [Consequences for People and Places](/research/consequences-for-people-and-places.html)

**Secondary connections:** [Where New Evidence Matters](/research/where-new-evidence-matters.html), [Modes of Climate Delivery](/research/modes-of-climate-delivery.html)

**Decision or problem:** How to represent locally varying benefits, burdens and costs without obscuring causal, geographic or valuation assumptions.

**Existing evidence:** The model separates baseline evidence, scenario actions, causal pathways, endpoints and valuation for traceable review.

**Consequential uncertainty:** Local evidence availability, causal assignment and valuation choices may materially change represented consequences.

**Delivery conditions:** Delivery and response assumptions remain separate so implementation conditions are not mistaken for outcome evidence.

**Consequences examined:** Health, equity and other place-based co-benefits, co-costs and distributional outcomes.

**Evidence status:** Owner-approved programme description; the model remains in development and provisional internal findings are not public conclusions.

**Claim boundaries:** Scenarios are conditional appraisals, not forecasts, predictions or universal transferability claims.

**Next learning question:** Which local evidence, delivery and valuation choices most alter scenario conclusions?

### Research facets

**Geographies:** canada, united-kingdom<br>
**Climate domains:** mitigation<br>
**Sectors:** buildings, transport, health<br>
**Methods:** place-based-modelling, economic-appraisal, distributional-analysis

## Research questions

- How can local climate scenarios represent co-benefits and co-costs without obscuring causal assumptions?
- How should evidence, geography and valuation choices be governed and traced?
